root_cause.text: The `vrealloc_node_align_noprof` function unconditionally copies `old_size` bytes of data from the old buffer to the newly allocated buffer of `size` bytes, failing to account for cases where the allocation is being shrunk (`size < old_size`).
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that `memcpy(n, p, old_size)` was replaced with `memcpy(n, p, min(size, old_size))` in `mm/vmalloc.c`, and the CVE description states: "If the request is to shrink the object (size < old_size), this results in an out-of-bounds write on the new buffer."

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent out-of-bounds memory access during reallocation shrinking by copying only the minimum of the old and new sizes.
intent_record.what: The third argument of the memcpy call is changed from 'old_size' to 'min(size, old_size)'.
intent_record.how: This limits the copied byte count to the smaller of the old and new sizes, preventing out-of-bounds memory access when the allocation is shrunk.
